newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks seen soft, Creative underpinned.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks seen soft, Creative underpinned.

text.p: Singapore shares were seen kicking the week off on a soft note in line with the weaker Wall Street close on Friday, dealers said.
They added Friday's rumours that Morgan Stanley Capital International's (MSCI) would re-weight regional stocks markets, including Singapore, were unfounded.
Late on Friday, Capital International Perspective S.A., the Geneva-based manager and calculator of MSCI indices, announced plans were underway to create MSCI Value and Growth Indices.
Dealers said multimedia Creative Technology could see some gains on the back of the company's bullish performance.
Over the weekend, it announced net profit of US$44.2 million for the quarter ended March 31, 1997, beating analysts' forecasts.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended at 2,019.60 on Friday, down a modest 0.57. Wall Street ended down 53.38 points, at 6,738.87.
